title: Successor Array Cycle Detection
statement: A company's task scheduler links tasks together using a successor array `next`, where `next[i]` is the index of the task that runs after task i, or -1 if task i is the last task. Starting from task index `start`, determine whether following the chain of successors ever revisits a task (a cycle), which would mean the scheduler is stuck in an infinite loop. Return true if a cycle is reachable from `start`, or false if the chain terminates at -1. Use O(1) extra space (a fast/slow pointer walk), not a visited set.
hints: This is the classic linked-list cycle problem, just with the 'next pointer' stored as an array index instead of a node reference.
Move two pointers through the array at different speeds; if there's a cycle they must eventually land on the same index.
slow moves one step (next[slow]), fast moves two steps (next[next[fast]]); stop early if fast hits -1 or next[fast] is -1; return True if slow ever equals fast.
